# worktree

Git worktree listing, creation, locking, removal and status.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-worktree.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-worktree.el)
- **Loaded:** by default
- **Requires:** [project](project.md)
- **Required by:** [commit-msg](commit-msg.md)
- **Brings along:** [ui-worktree](ui-worktree.md) (its UI)

## About

Sessions can live in a git worktree so parallel agents never step on
each other's working copy.  This module wraps the handful of git
commands that manage worktrees.  Every method is asynchronous: git
runs through `harness-run-command` and the method returns a promise
that resolves with parsed output or rejects with git's stderr.

Nothing here touches sessions; the session module gives a session
created with `:worktree PATH` that path as its cwd, and the merge
module merges a worktree's branch back into its parent's cwd.
Whatever else runs from a worktree lets go of it in the
`worktree/before-remove` filter, which `worktree/remove` runs before
git deletes the directory: the Emacs that `open_harness` started
there, say (harness-tools-dev.el).

Locks.  Every worktree the harness creates is locked (`git worktree
add --lock'), its lock reason starting with
`harness-worktree-lock-prefix`.  git never prunes a locked worktree,
and that matters because agents run git in a sandbox that shows only
their own worktree: a `git worktree prune` there takes every other
worktree for deleted and drops its registration, leaving its files
without an index and every git command in it failing.  The merge
module lifts the lock once the branch is merged (`worktree/unlock`),
so merged worktrees can be pruned again; `worktree/remove` lifts the
harness's lock itself.  Worktrees made before the harness locked them
are locked once per repository when the harness starts
(`worktree/lock-existing`).  Locks with another reason belong to
someone else and are left alone.

Merged worktrees.  The merge queue lifts a merged worktree's lock but
leaves the directory, so the harness's worktrees accumulate.  A merge
lands as one squash commit, whose branch tip is not in the target's
history, so git ancestry alone no longer says which worktrees merged:
the merge queue's `merge/finished` event records the child's worktree
in `harness-worktree--merged-file`, and `worktree/prune-merged`
removes the recorded (or still-ancestor) worktrees that are clean,
unlocked and used by no working session.

## Provides

### Methods

- `worktree/branch` (path) — Return a promise of the branch checked out at PATH, or nil when detached.
- `worktree/create` (root &rest opts) — Create a worktree of the repository at ROOT; return a promise of its plist.
- `worktree/list` (root) — Return a promise of the worktrees of the repository at ROOT.
- `worktree/lock` (root path &optional reason) — Lock the worktree at PATH of the repository at ROOT; return a promise.
- `worktree/lock-existing` (root) — Lock the worktrees the harness keeps for ROOT that have no lock yet.
- `worktree/prune` (root) — Prune stale worktree records of the repository at ROOT.
- `worktree/prune-merged` (root &optional dry-run) — Remove the worktrees of ROOT whose work has already merged.
- `worktree/remove` (root path &optional force) — Remove the worktree at PATH from the repository at ROOT.
- `worktree/root-of` (path) — Return a promise of the main repository root for PATH.
- `worktree/status` (path) — Return a promise of (:dirty BOOL :ahead N :behind N :branch NAME) for PATH.
- `worktree/unlock` (root path &optional any) — Unlock the worktree at PATH of the repository at ROOT; return a promise.

### Events

- `worktree/created` — (ROOT WORKTREE) after a worktree was added.
- `worktree/locked` — (ROOT PATH) after the harness locked a worktree.
- `worktree/removed` — (ROOT PATH) after a worktree was removed.
- `worktree/unlocked` — (ROOT PATH) after the harness unlocked a worktree.

### Filter chains it runs

- `worktree/before-remove`
- `worktree/lock-existing-p`

### Options

- `harness-worktree-branch-prefix` — Prefix of branch names generated for new worktrees.
- `harness-worktree-directory-function` — Function returning the directory for a new worktree.

## Uses

### Methods it calls

- `session/get` ([session](session.md)), when it is loaded
- `session/list` ([session](session.md)), when it is loaded

### Events it handles

- `harness/reloaded` → `harness-worktree--lock-known`
- `harness/started` → `harness-worktree--lock-known`
- `merge/finished` → `harness-worktree--on-merge-finished`
- `worktree/removed` → `harness-worktree--on-worktree-removed`

### Events it emits

- `worktree/created`
- `worktree/locked`
- `worktree/removed`
- `worktree/unlocked`
